claim: Untrusted artifact HTML (and raw HTML enabled by Markdown rendering) is stored and served as executable markup on the hub's own origin without isolation or sanitization.
trigger: An authenticated publisher submits HTML containing a script or event handler, or Markdown containing raw HTML such as <script>, and any reader opens /a/{artifact_id} (or /raw, /v/{version}, or the HTML source path).
impact: The supplied script executes with the artifact URL's same-origin privileges. In a browser tab where /admin has stored X-StorageApi-Token and X-Storage-Stack in sessionStorage, it can read those credentials and exfiltrate them; it can also issue same-origin requests as the reader. Password protection only gates delivery and does not make delivered HTML an isolated origin.

evidence.detail: src/builder.py:356-362 configures MarkdownIt with html=True; src/builder.py:484-494 renders Markdown into the page without sanitizing raw HTML.

src/main.py:1460-1470 returns HTMLResponse(envelope.html) for /a/{artifact_id}/raw; src/main.py:1561-1573 does the same for version pages; src/main.py:1499-1500 returns HTMLResponse(envelope.html) for HTML source.
src/pages.py:516-521 and 555-562 persist the owner Storage token and stack in same-origin sessionStorage; src/pages.py:581-585 attaches them to API requests.

expected_behavior_source: The admin UI's own security text states the Storage token is kept in sessionStorage, while artifact HTML is explicitly user-supplied and served as-is; a browser boundary should prevent artifact content from reading admin credentials.
suggested_fix: Serve artifacts from a distinct origin or sandboxed iframe; otherwise sanitize content and remove same-origin access to credential-bearing admin state.

snippet:
<script src="__HLJS_JS__"></script>

import mermaid from "__MERMAID_ESM__";

claim: Markdown artifacts depend on executable JavaScript fetched from mutable third-party CDN URLs without CSP restriction or subresource integrity.
trigger: A reader opens any Markdown or git-Markdown artifact and the browser successfully fetches the configured Highlight.js or Mermaid CDN resources; a CDN compromise, cache poisoning, or unexpected dependency update then changes the code executed in the artifact page.
impact: Compromised CDN JavaScript executes in the artifact page's origin and can inspect page content and make same-origin requests. It widens the trusted computing base for every rendered artifact and compounds the credential exposure risk when a user also has an admin session in the same origin.

evidence.detail: src/builder.py:93-104 defines Highlight.js and Mermaid URLs on cdn.jsdelivr.net/jsDelivr npm without version integrity metadata; src/builder.py:325-332 substitutes those values into every PAGE_TEMPLATE.
src/builder.py:484-494 and 804-862 build Markdown and git-Markdown artifacts through PAGE_TEMPLATE; src/main.py:1467-1470 serves the resulting HTML directly.

expected_behavior_source: The rendered artifact template is the implemented browser response contract for Markdown artifacts; executable third-party resources should be integrity-pinned or excluded from the artifact origin.
suggested_fix: Self-host and pin dependencies, add SRI hashes, and enforce a restrictive CSP on artifact responses (ideally from a separate origin).
